read: full: main text pp. 1-10 read in full; references and appendices (pp. 11-43) checked by keyword search for any language-model evaluation (none found)
venue_now: Preprint, arXiv v2, 11 Aug 2025 (p. 1); papers.json records the NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks Track, which this text does not show
what_it_is: EngiBench (Felten et al.) is an open-source Python library and set of datasets for data-driven engineering design optimisation. Each problem pairs a physics simulator with a dataset of designs, conditions and objective values behind a unified API (pp. 1-2, 5). Its seven problems cover airfoil shape optimisation (RANS CFD), 2D and 3D heat-conduction topology optimisation, thermoelastic and structural beam topology optimisation, photonics and power electronics (Table 1, p. 7). A companion library, EngiOpt, supplies baselines (GANs, diffusion models, MLP surrogates with NSGA-II). They are compared on similarity (MMD), diversity (DPP), cumulative optimality gap, and the ratios of violated constraints and failed simulations (pp. 3-4, 8-9). It evaluates machine-learning optimisation and generative-design methods, not language models.
domain: machine learning for engineering design optimisation: aerodynamics, heat conduction, structural and thermoelastic topology optimisation, photonics, power electronics
size: 7 problem implementations with datasets (Table 1, p. 7); baseline algorithms in EngiOpt; 10 runs per algorithm-problem pair in the experiments (p. 8); no LLMs
source_of_items: generated by physics simulators and optimisers; several problems replicate setups from prior publications (p. 6)
instances: generated (simulation datasets of designs, not natural-language items)
has_gold_traces: no: the datasets hold designs, conditions and objective values; optimisers return optimisation histories (p. 5), not reasoning traces
evaluation: simulation-based metrics on generated designs: MMD similarity, DPP diversity, cumulative optimality gap, ratio of violated constraints, ratio of failed simulations (pp. 3-4)
human_validation: none reported as a study; the problem implementations are described as rigorously tested (p. 2) and were developed over 5-6 years at UMD (p. 10)
contamination_measures: none (not applicable: no language models are evaluated)

engtrace_use.sentence: Not cited in the text. The May reference entry for Zhou et al., 2025 (L1248-1249) adds: 'Distinct from the design-focused EngiBench by Felten et al.', and gives no entry for Felten et al.
engtrace_use.explanation: The note is right in substance. Felten et al.'s EngiBench is design-focused: it is a framework 'for data-driven engineering design research' (p. 1) that benchmarks generative and surrogate design methods (pp. 1-2, 8-9), and it is a different work from Zhou et al.'s LLM benchmark. The only flaw is bibliographic: the note names a work that has no reference entry.

suggested_wording: (If disambiguation is wanted, as a footnote: EngiBench (Zhou et al., 2025) is unrelated to the EngiBench library of Felten et al. (2025), which benchmarks machine-learning methods for simulation-based engineering design optimisation rather than language models.)

Baselines in the companion library EngiOpt include GANs, diffusion models and MLP surrogates with NSGA-II (pp. 1, 8)

overlap_with_engtrace: Shares only engineering subject matter and simulation-based checking of outputs. It is not an LLM benchmark: no natural-language items, no reasoning traces, no step-level or LLM evaluation, no contamination question. It does not belong in EngTrace's related work.
notes: Naming clash only. The in-text key 'EngiBench (Zhou et al., 2025)' and Zhou et al.'s full title already identify which EngiBench is meant. The May bibliography note should be deleted, or, if the writers keep the disambiguation as a footnote, backed by a proper entry (arXiv:2508.00831). Citing Felten et al. in the body would only add noise.
